requirements.lead_text: Family and Home Safety. Do the following:
requirements.req_text: Family and Home Safety. Do the following: (a) Explain common causes of and prevention of home injuries. (b) Discuss the dangers involved with the use of fireworks. (c) Explain common causes of and prevention of home fires. (d) Using the Home Safety Checklist in the Safety merit badge pamphlet, or one approved by your counselor, inspect your home or a similar building for hazards with an adult. Review your checklist and findings with your counselor. (e) Develop a fire-escape plan for your home or for a similar building. Include in your drawings exit routes from each room and a meeting place outside. Conduct a fire-escape drill. Review your plan and your drill with your counselor. (f) Develop a family emergency action plan for evacuation because of weather or other natural disasters that occur in your area. Using a checklist in the Safety merit badge pamphlet or one approved by your counselor, assemble or inspect an emergency supplies kit. Explain to your counselor how a family would use the plan and the kit supplies in an emergency.

sub_requirements.label: (a)
sub_requirements.text: Explain common causes of and prevention of home injuries.

requirements.req_text: Safeguarding Youth. Do the following: (a) Discuss Scouting America's Safeguarding Youth guidelines that adults and Scouts must follow so that everyone is safe at Scouting activities. (b) Discuss with your counselor what situations and behaviors would prompt you to Recognize, Resist, and Report a possible abuse situation. requirements.lead_text: Careers. Do ONE of the following:
requirements.req_text: Careers. Do ONE of the following: (a) Explore careers related to Safety merit badge. Research one career to learn about the training and education needed, costs, job prospects, salary, job duties, and career advancement. With permission of your parent or guardian, your research methods may include an internet or library search, an interview with a professional in the field, or a visit to a location where people in this career work. Discuss with your counselor both your findings and what about this profession might make it an interesting career. (b) Explore how you could use knowledge and skills related to safety to pursue a hobby, lifestyle, or service as a volunteer. Research any training needed, expenses, and organizations that promote or support it. Discuss with your counselor what short-term and long-term goals you might have if you pursue this.

sub_requirements.label: (a)
sub_requirements.text: Explore careers related to Safety merit badge. Research one career to learn about the training and education needed, costs, job prospects, salary, job duties, and career advancement. With permission of your parent or guardian, your research methods may include an internet or library search, an interview with a professional in the field, or a visit to a location where people in this career work. Discuss with your counselor both your findings and what about this profession might make it an interesting career.

sub_requirements.label: (b)
sub_requirements.text: Explore how you could use knowledge and skills related to safety to pursue a hobby, lifestyle, or service as a volunteer. Research any training needed, expenses, and organizations that promote or support it. Discuss with your counselor what short-term and long-term goals you might have if you pursue this.

pamphlet_excerpts: Safety Sub-Req 9a: Explore careers related to Safety merit badge. Research one career to learn about the training and education needed, costs, job prospects, salary, job duties.
Safety Sub-Req 9b: Explore how you could use knowledge and skills related to safety to pursue a hobby, lifestyle, or service as a volunteer. Research any training.
Core Standard 1 (Req 9): Do ONE of the following: (a) Explore careers related to Safety merit badge.
Core Standard 2 (Req 9): Research one career to learn about the training and education needed, costs, job prospects, salary, job duties, and career advancement.
step_by_step_procedure: Prepare & Inspect (Req 9): Review the official Safety requirement standard and verify all required tools, reference tables, and safety gear.
Analyze Core Principles: Identify the primary concepts, definitions, and cause-and-effect relationships governing Safety Careers, Training & Hobby Pathways.
Execute & Document: Perform the careers task methodically with your patrol buddy and log specific observations in your Safety Workbook.
Verify With Counselor: Present your completed work, demonstrate proficiency, and answer Socratic check-for-understanding questions for Blue Card sign-off.

Signed Blue Card (Application for Merit Badge #34124) or Scoutbook Digital Record

left_points: Skips pre-task hazard scan and relies on guesswork during Requirement 9.
Provides vague, one-word workbook notes without measurable field evidence.
Rushes past buddy verification and cannot explain why each step matters.
right_points: Completes a structured safety and equipment check before starting Requirement 9.
Records concrete measurements, examples, and citations from Official BSA Safety Pamphlet, pp. 52-57.
Demonstrates mastery using the BSA EDGE method (Explain, Demonstrate, Guide, Enable).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: During a patrol review of Safety Requirement 9, a Scout claims: "Listing three job titles from a web search satisfies the Safety career exploration requirement." How should you respond?
options: Agree with the claim so the patrol can finish the requirement faster
Correct the misconception: Scouts must research three Safety careers and discuss the specific education, training, licensing, and daily duties for one chosen career with their counselor.
Skip Requirement 9 until after the troop court of honor
Sign off the Blue Card without completing the practical verification
quiz_item.correct_answer: Option B - Correct the misconception: Scouts must research three Safety careers and discuss the specific education, training, licensing, and daily duties for one chosen career with their counselor.
quiz_item.explanation: Per Official BSA Safety Pamphlet, pp. 52-57, Scouts must research three Safety careers and discuss the specific education, training, licensing, and daily duties for one chosen career with their counselor.
